# Loading libraries
```{r, message=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(ggVennDiagram)
library(VennDiagram)
library(openxlsx)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggupset)
library(ggridges)
```

# Importing fibroblast datasets
```{r}
fibro <- read_xlsx('data/input/samp.xlsx')
fibro <- as.data.frame(fibro)

# Extract the gene name and set it as row names
fibro$protein <- gsub(".*GN=([A-Za-z0-9]+) .*", "\\1", fibro$protein)
rownames(fibro) <- fibro$protein

# Drop the original protein column without resetting row names
fibro <- subset(fibro, select = -protein)
```

# Load and subset supermere proteomics from Group Project
```{r, message=FALSE}
protein_data <- read_csv("./data/input/protein_data_normnoNCB.csv")
protein_data <- as.data.frame(protein_data, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(protein_data) <- protein_data$protein
#remove $protein column
protein_data <- protein_data[,-1]
#round up the data keeping only 2 decimal places
protein_data <- round(protein_data, 2)
superp <- protein_data[, c(7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18, 23, 24, 25, 26)]
```

# Merge two dfs
```{r}
# Ensure the rownames are set properly
superp$protein <- rownames(superp)
fibro$protein <- rownames(fibro)

# Merge the two dataframes by the 'protein' column
superfibro <- merge(superp, fibro, by = "protein", all = TRUE)

# Set the rownames to be the 'protein' column and remove the 'protein' column
rownames(superfibro) <- superfibro$protein
superfibro <- superfibro[, -which(colnames(superfibro) == "protein")]

# 'superfibro' now has 14 columns and all protein names are merged without duplicates
superfibro[is.na(superfibro)] <- 0

```

# Small version 

```{r}
superfibroxs  <- data.frame(
  DiFi2DUCSuper = rowMeans(superfibro[, 1:3], na.rm = TRUE),  # Average of columns 1-3
  DiFi3DUCSuper = rowMeans(superfibro[, 4:6], na.rm = TRUE),  # Average of columns 4-6
  DiFi_FPLCSuper = rowMeans(superfibro[, 7:10], na.rm = TRUE), # Average of columns 7-10
  HNPCC_S = superfibro[, 11]  # Column 13 as is
)

rownames(superfibroxs) <- rownames(superfibro)

# Filter out rows where all values are 0
superfibroxs[] <- lapply(superfibroxs, function(x) {
  as.numeric(as.character(x))  # Convert factors or characters to numeric
})
superfibroxs_filtered <- superfibroxs[!apply(superfibroxs, 1, function(x) all(x == 0)), ]

# Step 1: Check for rows where all values are effectively zero (accounting for small values)
zero_rows <- apply(superfibroxs, 1, function(row) {
  all(abs(row) < .Machine$double.eps)  # Check if all values are close to 0
})

# Print the number of rows that are all effectively zero
num_zero_rows <- sum(zero_rows)
cat("Number of rows where all values are effectively zero:", num_zero_rows, "\n")

# Step 2: Filter out those rows
superfibroxs_filtered <- superfibroxs[!zero_rows, ]

# Check the structure of the filtered data
str(superfibroxs_filtered)

# Optionally, display the first few rows of the filtered data frame
head(superfibroxs_filtered)
```
# Make a Venn with Venndiagramm
```{r}
# Create a list of proteins that are non-zero in each column
# You can replace the sample column names with actual names if you have them
sets <- list(
  DiFi_2D_UC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 1] != 0, ]),
  DiFi_3D_UC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 2] != 0, ]),
  DiFi_3D_FPLC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 3] != 0, ]),
  SAMP = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 4] != 0, ])
)

grpsets <- list(DiFi_2D_UC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 1] != 0, ]),
  DiFi_3D_UC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 2] != 0, ]),
  DiFi_3D_FPLC = rownames(superfibroxs_filtered[superfibroxs_filtered[, 3] != 0, ])
  )
# Create the Venn diagram
venn.plot <- venn.diagram(
  x = sets,
  category.names = names(sets),  # Custom names for the categories (samples)
  filename = NULL,                # Set to NULL to plot directly
  output = TRUE,
  lwd = 2,                       # Line width
  col = "black",                 # Line color
  fill = c("lightblue", "blue", "darkgreen", "yellow"),  # Fill colors for each circle
  alpha = 0.5,                   # Transparency level
  cat.cex = 1.5,                 # Size of category names
  cat.pos = 0,                   # Position of category names
  cat.dist = 0.05                # Distance of category names from the circles
)

grid.draw(venn.plot)

```

# Searching for a specific protein within the dataset
```{r}
# Search for 'DDR1' in each element of the list 'sets'
result <- sapply(sets, function(x) 'DDR1' %in% x)

# Print the result
result

```
# Make a venn with ggplot

```{r}
#Convert the data to a list of vectors

dataset_list <- lapply(superfibroxs, as.vector)
#Plot basic ggVennDiagram and set the catergory names manually

venn2 <- ggVennDiagram(sets)
#Save Venn to pdf retaining the dimensions ggsave("DiFi.pdf", plot = venn, device = "pdf", width = 12, height = 10)
vennS <- ggVennDiagram(sets[1:3])
#Extract plotting data from venn and write it in Excel file
write.xlsx(process_region_data(Venn(sets)),file = "venn_proteins_SAMP.xlsx", rowNames = FALSE)
venn2
```
# Make an upset plot with ggplot

```{r}
ggVennDiagram(sets, force_upset = TRUE) -> upset2
upset2
```

# Print all 4 set intersection data

```{r}
alls <- overlap(Venn(sets), 1:4)
alls
```
